meta.title: start-from-here — plan first, then build with any AI coding agent
meta.description: An open Agent Skill that interviews you and writes approved project docs (PRD, architecture, database, security, tests, legal, AGENTS.md) before your AI agent writes any code. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Copilot, Cursor and 30+ tools.

why.title: Why plan before you prompt?
why.lead: “Vibe coding” — asking an AI to build an app straight from a one-line idea — feels fast. But the agent has to guess.
why.p1_body: Scope, users, data model, permissions, security rules and conventions are all invented on the fly. Every guess becomes code.
why.p2_body: Wrong guesses surface late — after the schema, the auth flow and the UI are built on top of them.
why.p3_body: A new session, a new model or a new teammate starts from zero, because nothing was written down.
why.s1_body: Short rounds of numbered questions, each with a labeled recommended default. Beginners can say “use your recommendations”; experts can skip ahead.
why.s2_body: No stack yet? You get 2–3 options with trade-offs and one marked Recommended. Nothing is final until you approve it.
why.s3_body: Shared IDs (F-01, NFR-01, ADR-0001…) link every document, and a final audit cross-checks them.
why.s4_body: Unknowns become [TBD], ideas become PROPOSAL, guesses become ASSUMPTION. It never claims your project “is compliant”.
why.s5_body: Its job ends with approved documents, a readiness checklist and a first implementation prompt for any coding agent.

how.title: How it works
how.lead: Eight phases with explicit gates. The skill stops at every gate and waits for your answer.
how.p0_desc: New project, existing repo, resume or doc update? Can it write files here?
how.p1_desc: Language, experience, idea and size. Proposes a tier and the doc list.
how.p2_desc: Rounds of up to 7 questions, each with a recommended default.
how.p3_desc: 2–3 stack, hosting or license options with trade-offs.
how.p4_desc: Writes docs/DISCOVERY.md and shows a short summary.
how.p5_desc: Writes docs in dependency order, in review batches.
how.p6_desc: Cross-checks scope, names, stack, roles, NFRs, legal and links.
how.p7_desc: Readiness checklist, open questions and a first implementation prompt.
how.f1_body: Progress is saved to docs/.start-from-here/STATE.md after every step. In any tool, with any model, say “resume”.
how.f2_body: In an existing repo it inspects manifests, CI and docs first, then proposes section-level merges. It never overwrites files.
how.f3_body: In chat-only tools each document arrives as a path heading plus a Markdown block, two or three per message. Reply “next” for more.
how.f4_body: Chat in one language and write the docs in another — for example chat in Indonesian, docs in English. IDs and file names stay in English.

docs.title: What you get
docs.lead: These files are generated inside your project. Which ones you get depends on the tier and your answers (UI? personal data? API? open source?).
docs.legal_note: Drafts for review by qualified counsel — not legal advice.
docs.discovery: Interview record: answers, assumptions and decisions. The source of truth.
docs.docs_readme: Docs index with a Draft / Approved status table.
docs.prd: Vision, personas, features with acceptance criteria, success metrics.
docs.app_flow: Screens, commands or endpoints, user flows and states.
docs.design_system: Design tokens, components, states and accessibility.
docs.trd: Feature-to-technical mapping and measurable non-functional requirements.
docs.architecture: C4 context and container diagrams, stack table, data flow.
docs.database: Entities, ERD, schema, access rules, migrations and retention.
docs.api: Contract conventions, endpoints, RPCs or CLI, errors and versioning.
docs.security: STRIDE threat model, authentication/authorization matrix, secrets and privacy.
docs.testing: Test strategy and an acceptance matrix linked to features and NFRs.
docs.operations: Environments, CI/CD, deploy and rollback, SLOs, backup and incidents.
docs.impl_plan: Milestones and ordered tasks, each with a definition of done.
docs.adr: Architecture decision records (MADR), one per major decision.
docs.agents_md: Universal instructions for any AI coding agent; links every doc.
docs.pointers: Optional thin pointer files to AGENTS.md for specific tools.
docs.code_style: Conventions, project structure and verified commands.
docs.ai_guidelines: AI coding dos and don'ts, prompt hygiene, reviewing AI code.
docs.git_workflow: Branching, Conventional Commits, PR review and releases.
docs.license: Full official license text — never paraphrased.
docs.terms: Terms of service, if you have accounts or a SaaS.
docs.privacy: Privacy policy, if you process any personal data.
docs.cookie: Cookie policy, if a website uses tracking.
docs.compliance: Regulatory register: regimes, controls and owners.
docs.oss_files: README, CHANGELOG, CONTRIBUTING, CODE_OF_CONDUCT, SECURITY, SUPPORT, ACCESSIBILITY, CODEOWNERS, PR and issue templates.
docs.threat_note: The threat model lives in docs/technical/SECURITY_ARCHITECTURE.md. Root SECURITY.md is reserved for GitHub's vulnerability-disclosure policy.

tiers.title: Tiers
tiers.lead: The skill proposes a tier from what it learns, and you confirm it. You can switch individual documents on or off at any time.
tiers.lite_for: Solo, indie, prototype, hackathon, internal tool
tiers.std_for: Startup MVP, open-source project, small-team product
tiers.ent_for: Regulated data, multiple teams, SLAs, multi-tenant, audits
tiers.note: Any regulated-data signal (health, payments, children, finance) makes the skill propose Enterprise unless you object. Say “change tier Standard” later to recompute the document set.

modes.title: Experience modes
modes.lead: Chosen in the first round, or inferred from how you write.
modes.beginner_body: Explains every technical term in one plain sentence. Always recommends. Prefers multiple choice. No unexplained acronyms.
modes.intermediate_body: Short explanations of less common terms. Recommendations with one-line trade-offs.
modes.expert_body: Terse. Shows trade-offs and alternatives. Accepts free-form answers.
modes.tip: Not sure what something means? Say “explain ERD” (or any term) at any time.

install.title: Install on your platform
install.lead: Pick your tool. Every command comes from the official platform guides in this repository.
install.skills_title: Vercel skills CLI — installs for every agent it detects
install.skills_body: The fastest route when you have Node 22.20 or newer. Add -g for a global install or -a <agent> to target one agent.
install.ours_body: Works on Node 18+. With no --agent it installs to .agents/skills (read by most agents) plus .claude/skills. It copies by default, never overwrites without --force and supports --dry-run.
install.gh_body: No Node? gh 2.90 or newer can install skills directly from the repository and pin a version.
install.claude_body: Add the marketplace and install the plugin inside Claude Code, or install the plain skill with one of the CLIs.
install.codex_body: Install as a skill (project .agents/skills or global) or add the plugin marketplace.
install.gemini_body: Install as an extension (adds a /start-from-here command) or as a plain skill. Gemini asks for consent before activating a skill.
install.zip_title: Claude.ai, Claude Desktop and skill upload
install.zip_body: Download start-from-here.zip from the latest GitHub release and upload it.
install.zip_s2: Click + › Create skill › Upload a skill.
install.zip_s3: Choose start-from-here.zip and make sure the skill is toggled on.
install.zip_s4: Say: “Use the start-from-here skill to plan my new app.”
install.chatgpt_body: Use Skills (beta, business plans) when available; otherwise build a Custom GPT or a Project from the release files.
install.chatgpt_s1: Skills (beta): Plugins › Skills › Create › Upload from your computer › start-from-here.zip.
install.chatgpt_s2: Custom GPT: Explore GPTs › Create › Configure. Paste gpt-instructions.md into Instructions.
install.chatgpt_s3: Upload every file from the knowledge zip under Knowledge, then save.
install.gems_body: Gems have no filesystem, so the skill runs from instructions plus knowledge files.
install.gems_s1: Go to gemini.google.com › Gems › New Gem and name it start-from-here.
install.gems_s3: Upload the files from knowledge-txt/ in the knowledge zip (up to 10 files).
install.gems_s4: Save, open the Gem and type “start”.
install.copilot_title: GitHub Copilot (CLI, cloud agent, VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains)
install.copilot_body: Copilot reads .agents/skills. Install with gh, the skills CLI or our installer.
install.cursor_body: Cursor reads .agents/skills in the project, or ~/.cursor/skills globally. Invoke it in Agent chat.
install.others_title: Cline, Roo, Kilo, Junie, Kiro, Zed, OpenCode, Goose, Amp and more
install.others_body: Use our installer with the agent id. Run list-agents to see every id and its paths.
install.local_title: Local and other LLMs (Ollama, LM Studio, Le Chat, DeepSeek, Grok…)
install.local_body: No filesystem? Paste start-from-here.prompt.md from the latest release into the chat or the system prompt, then say “start”.
install.local_s1: Download start-from-here.prompt.md from the latest release.
install.local_s2: Paste it as the system prompt (or as the first message, followed by “Follow these instructions for this conversation”).
install.local_s3: For Ollama, bake it into a Modelfile:
install.manual_body: Clone the repository and copy the skill folder into your project.

compat.title: Compatibility
compat.lead: Native skill support means the tool loads SKILL.md folders on demand. Rules-file fallback and prompt-only tools still work — just with a different install route.
compat.unverified_note: Agents whose paths are known only from third-party sources are marked UNVERIFIED by list-agents.

usage.title: Usage & quick commands
usage.lead: Say these at any time. Loose wording works too (“continue”, “you decide”).
usage.start_tip: Add your idea on the same line to save a round, e.g. /start-from-here a booking app for my yoga studio.
usage.c_resume: Read the saved state and continue where you left off.
usage.c_status: Show phase, tier, document status and open questions.
usage.c_recs: Accept every recommended default in this round; each is recorded as an ASSUMPTION.
usage.c_skip: Fill unanswered areas with labeled assumptions and go to the brief approval gate.
usage.c_audit: Run only the consistency audit on existing docs.
usage.c_update: Edit that doc, then update every document that depends on the change.
usage.c_add: Generate one extra document from the catalog.
usage.c_tier: Recompute the document set, show the difference and wait for approval.
usage.c_next: Chat-only mode: send the next batch of documents.
usage.check_body: Finds missing files, leftover placeholders, broken links and broken ID cross-references (undefined or duplicate IDs, untested Must features) in a generated project.

example.title: Example session
example.lead: A beginner plans a booking app in Claude Code. Abridged.
example.l1: /start-from-here a booking app for my yoga studio
example.l2: Phase 0 — new project, I can write files here. Round 0 (5 questions): 1. Language for chat and docs? Recommended: English. 2. Your experience? 3. Who books — only your students, or the public? 4. Payments online or at the studio? Recommended: at the studio for v1. 5. Just you, or a team? Unsure? Say “use your recommendations”.
example.l3: beginner, public, at the studio for now, just me. use your recommendations for the rest.
example.l4: Proposed tier: Lite (solo, no regulated data). Docs: DISCOVERY, PRD, APP_FLOW, ARCHITECTURE, DATABASE, SECURITY_ARCHITECTURE (short), TESTING, CODE_STYLE, AI_GUIDELINES, IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN, PRIVACY_POLICY, AGENTS.md, README, LICENSE. STOP — approve this tier and list, or change it.
example.l5: Phase 7 — Handoff. Readiness: 11 ready · 2 warnings (open questions Q-03, Q-05) · 0 blocking. Here is your first implementation prompt. Paste it into any coding agent.
example.prompt_body: The skill stops at handoff. Paste this into any coding agent — it doesn't need the skill, because it reads AGENTS.md and the docs it links.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.a1: No. It writes planning documents only. Small illustrative snippets inside docs (a config key name, a command already verified in your repo) are allowed, but no application code, packages, migrations or deployments.
faq.q2: Which AI model do I need?
faq.a2: Any capable model. The skill is model-agnostic plain Markdown that follows the open Agent Skills standard, and it also ships as a single pasteable prompt for chat-only tools and local models.
faq.q3: Can I use it on an existing project?
faq.a3: Yes. In brownfield mode it inspects manifests, CI and existing docs first, records current facts as “as-is” and plans as “to-be”, and proposes section-level merges instead of overwriting files.
faq.q4: Will it invent facts or claim compliance?
faq.a4: No. Unknowns are written as [TBD: question — owner], ideas as PROPOSAL and guesses as ASSUMPTION. Legal documents are drafts marked “not legal advice”, and it never states your project is compliant.
faq.q5: Do I have to answer every question?
faq.a5: No. Every question has a recommended default. Say “use your recommendations” for a whole round, or “skip to generation” to fill the gaps with labeled assumptions.
faq.q6: What if my session ends halfway?
faq.a6: Progress is saved to docs/.start-from-here/STATE.md after every step. Open any tool with any model and say “resume”. In chat-only tools, save the state block yourself and attach it.
faq.a7: The skill is a set of local files with no network calls of its own. Your conversation goes wherever your AI tool sends it. The skill never writes secrets — if you paste one, it tells you to rotate it.
faq.q8: Which install method should I pick?
faq.a8: Terminal agent with Node 22.20+: npx skills add. Older Node: npx start-from-here install. Claude Code, Codex or Gemini CLI with auto-updates: the plugin or extension. Chat apps: upload the zip, or paste the prompt file.
faq.a9: Re-run your install command with --force (our installer), npx skills update, or update the plugin or extension. Your generated documents are never touched by an update.
faq.a10: Yes. It is open source under the MIT license. You only pay for the AI tool you already use.
faq.q11: My AI has a small context window (local LLM, small model). Will it work?
faq.a11: Yes — use session mode. Say “session mode” and the work is split into short work packages, one per fresh session, connected by a handover file (docs/.start-from-here/HANDOVER.md) that keeps decisions and IDs consistent. The skill proposes it automatically for local or small models and long projects.
